messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT fired for service hosted-inference-prod (SEV=high) — 5xx rate spike in us-west-2. PagerDuty incident pd_2026_3999 created: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/pd_2026_3999. Symptoms: ~12% 5xx over baseline in last 2m, elevated queue depth on inference-runtime. Escalation policy: prod-oncall.
PagerDuty: Escalation policy 'prod-oncall' triggered. Primary (Alex H) contacted via push/SMS/phone — no ACK within 90s. Secondary (Sanjay P) paged. Manager (Leah C) will be paged if no ACK from secondary in 3m. Incident priority: P1.
Maria T: seeing a big spike in request rate from a single client IP range and an internal scheduled job "demo-bench" ramping up. Graphs: https://grafana.example/d/inferrun/hosted-inference-prod?panel=5
Chris L: confirmed, the KV cache RTT and memory usage are climbing. Noticed repeated prefix cache misses. Might be a thundering-burst from the bench job.
Alex H: sorry folks — I was driving and phone was on DND, didn't get the push. I see PD shows I timed out. I'm back online now, but won't take primary unless you want me to.
PagerDuty: Secondary (Sanjay P) acknowledged the incident at +00:02. Escalation to manager suppressed.
Sanjay P: I'm on it. Spinning up extra replicas and throttling bench traffic. Taking traffic off the hot hosts.
Sanjay P: running:
```
kubectl -n inference scale deploy inference-runtime --replicas=8
kubectl patch deployment inference-runtime -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"rollback-safe":"true"}}}}}'
# apply temporary rate-limit on demo-bench job
kubectl -n tools patch cronjob demo-bench -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'
```
OpsBot: Command output: scaled to 8 replicas, patch applied, cronjob suspended. New pods are initializing (3/3 ready in 45s).
Maria T: after scaling, 5xx rate dropped to ~1.6% within 90s. Latency still slightly elevated for long-tail (p95 up ~220ms).
Chris L: checking logs — one host had repeated OOMs related to KV cache growth, suspect memory leak under certain query patterns. Dumped heap and uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-dumps/inference/3999999999/heap-1.hprof
Alex H: big customer impact check — support reports two paying customers (CUST-224, CUST-198) saw intermittent 503s between 09:12-09:18 UTC. Support has been notified.
Sanjay P: confirming mitigation: suspended bench, scaled up, and rolling restart of hot hosts. Will remove the problematic model shard from those nodes as next step.
Leah C: got paged as manager escalation briefly — saw PD fire the manager rule then suppressed after secondary ACK. Thanks for taking lead, Sanjay. Keep me posted if we need a bridge or customer-facing comms.
Sanjay P: creating a private bridge now: https://zoom.example/bridge/inf-3999999999 (ops creds). Chris, can you do the shard remap?
Chris L: on it. remapping model shards off host-3 and host-5. That should relieve KV ballooning.
PagerDuty: Note: primary ack now recorded by Alex H at +00:04 (manual). No further escalation.
Maria T: recommend follow-ups: 1) block demo-bench from prod (suspend permanently or move to staging), 2) add circuit-breaker on KV cache, 3) add PD rule for SMS fallback to manager earlier (some PD users missed push).
Alex H: agree. Also suggest we add a monitoring alert for per-host KV cache growth rate to catch this earlier.
Leah C: I don't need to join the mitigation bridge for now. Please post a short incident summary when resolved and tag me, ops, and eng-runtime.
Sanjay P: svc recovered to normal error rates at +00:06. Will keep the extra replicas for 30m then scale down. Taking incident to resolved state in PD after postmortem notes.
IncidentBot: Incident pd_2026_3999: RESOLVED — root cause mitigation applied (bench suspended, scaled replicas, shard remap). Impact: temporary 5xx spike; two customers saw intermittent 503s. Follow-ups: postmortem, PD escalation policy review, KV cache alerting. Assigned owners: Chris L (root cause investigation), Maria T (alerts/remediation), Alex H (PD policy changes). :white_check_mark:
